notes: TBox rule edit. Derivability very_unlikely: see evidence. Two determinate queries on new members named in the prompt (the rule is the only route) and two background-belief queries on well-known members whose value a model may store by name. Following the README and the coordinator's ruling, in a world where the stored value wins, the member's bird membership gives way; it never becomes an exception to the edited rule (that would be the inconsistent patch). The two members' storage choices are independent, so four worlds. R1: every bird species lays eggs; there are no viviparous birds. The well-known members are the two flightless birds, whose bird membership is the one a model could most plausibly give up; the chicken was avoided because 'the chicken is not a bird' is barely a coherent world. The new members are real, little-known species (verified on Wikipedia).
